prompt: A flat, straight-on digital image of a generic Indian real-estate promotional flyer for a new residential high-rise project, as it looks when forwarded on WhatsApp: slight JPEG softness, filling the whole frame edge to edge, no phone frame, no hands, no table. Portrait layout in a navy-blue and warm-gold palette on an off-white ground. Top to bottom: (1) from about 4% to 19% of the height, a very large bold two-line headline in navy, left-aligned; (2) from 19% to 24%, one thinner line of sub-headline text; (3) from 25% to 58%, a glossy architectural rendering of two modern residential towers with balconies, landscaped gardens and a blue sky, with a round gold starburst sticker overlapping the rendering's top-right corner (about 65% to 95% across, 26% to 38% down) carrying two short words; (4) from 59% to 70%, a full-width navy price ribbon with one very large figure on its left side and a smaller line of text on its right third; (5) from 72% to 83%, a row of four simple gold line icons in circles (a swimming pool, a dumbbell, a tree, a building), each with a short caption below; (6) from 86% to 96%, a pale strip with three lines of tiny fine print on the left and a small plain empty square at the far right. Every letter and number must be completely illegible: soft, smudged pseudo-text that reads as printed type from a distance but contains no real words, digits or names. No logos, no brand names, no developer or broker names, no phone numbers, no QR codes, no government emblems or seals, no people.

Street-level documentary photograph in Gurugram, India, on a hazy winter morning. A long printed construction-site hoarding (a billboard panel on the site's boundary wall), shot nearly straight on, spans the full width of the frame across its middle band, from about 35% to 70% of the image height. Above it rises a residential tower under construction, with bare concrete floors and a tower crane; below it is a dusty footpath with a parked scooter at one edge. The hoarding is navy and warm gold. On its left half: a very large two-line headline at the top (about 37% to 47% of the image height), a medium single line below it (about 49% to 56%), and a thin strip of small print along the hoarding's bottom edge (about 61% to 67%). On its right half: a printed rendering of finished glass-and-concrete towers. All text on the hoarding is completely illegible: smudged pseudo-letters with no real words, numbers or names. Natural light, honest and unretouched, like a buyer's own phone photo. No logos, no brand names, no developer names, no government emblems or seals, no QR codes, no phone numbers, no readable signage, no faces.
